subject: Commerce
preamble: There will be two papers, Paper 1 and Paper 2, both of which will constitute a composite paper to be taken at one sitting.
aims: assess candidates' understanding of the fundamental concepts, scope, and functions of commerce and e-commerce;
evaluate candidates' knowledge of occupations, production processes, and forms of business units;
test candidates' understanding of commercial capital, profits, trade associations, and channels of distribution;
assess candidates' familiarity with home and foreign trade procedures, documentation, and international economic groupings;
evaluate candidates' knowledge of financial systems, marketing concepts, legal aspects of business, and business management.

examination_scheme.summary: There will be two papers, Paper 1 and Paper 2, both of which will constitute a composite paper to be taken at one sitting.

papers.title: Multiple Choice Objective Test
papers.details: A 50-minute test consisting of fifty multiple choice questions drawn from the entire syllabus.

papers.title: Essay Paper
papers.details: A 2-hour essay-type test consisting of eight questions. Candidates will be required to answer any five questions.

topics.title: 1. Introduction to Commerce
topics.notes: Definition, scope, functions, and historical background of Commerce and E-Commerce.

topics.title: 2. Occupation
topics.notes: Meaning and types (Industrial, Commercial, Service); factors determining choice of occupation and career opportunities.

topics.title: 3. Production
topics.notes: Meaning, factors (Land, Labour, Capital, Entrepreneurship), and types (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary); division of labour/specialization (types, advantages, disadvantages, limitations); inter-relationship between production and exchange.

topics.title: 4. Business Units
topics.notes: Meaning and objectives of business; forms (Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Co-operative Societies, Credit Union & Thrift Societies, Public Enterprises, Companies); characteristics, formation, capital sources, advantages, and disadvantages; amalgamations, mergers, acquisitions, trusts, holding companies, cartels, and consortiums; dissolution/liquidation procedures.

topics.title: 5. Trade Associations
topics.notes: Aims and functions of Trade Associations, Chambers of Commerce, Employers' Associations, and Consumer Associations/Consumerism.

topics.title: 6. Business Capital and Profits
topics.notes: Meaning and types of capital (Authorized, Called-up, Paid-up, Liquid, Capital Owned); credit sources, instruments, and functions; calculation and importance of working capital, profits (gross and net), and turnover.

topics.title: 7. Home and Foreign Trade
topics.notes: Purpose and branches of trade; Home trade (retail and wholesale types, functions, trends, elimination/survival of middlemen, channels of distribution); Foreign trade (types, basic concepts like terms of trade and balance of payments, barriers, tariffs, functions of port/customs authorities and export promotion councils).

topics.title: 8. Purchase and Sale of Goods
topics.notes: Procedures and documentation (Indent, Invoices, Credit/Debit notes, Letters of hypothecation, Certificates of origin/inspection); price quotations (discounts, COD, CWO, CIF, FOB, Ex-works, E&OE); terms and means of payment (legal tender, cheques, standing orders, bills of exchange, electronic payments).

topics.title: 9. Finance and Financial Institutions
topics.notes: Money (evolution, forms, functions); Banking (Central Bank, Commercial Banks, E-banking, accounts, Bureau-de-Change); Insurance (principles, life/non-life, insurable/uninsurable risks, underwriting, reinsurance); Capital and Stock Markets (raising funds, shares, stocks, bonds, speculators, second-tier securities market); Commodity Exchanges (requirements, trading methods, benefits).

topics.title: 10. Transport, Tourism, Communication and Warehousing
topics.notes: Transport (importance, forms, choices, documentation like waybills and manifests); Tourism (advantages and disadvantages); Communication (types, post office, courier, e-mail/internet, computer appreciation); Warehousing (importance, functions, types, advantages).

topics.title: 11. Advertising
topics.notes: Meaning, roles, types (informative, persuasive, competitive), methods (direct/indirect), and media selection.

topics.title: 12. Marketing and Customer Service
topics.notes: Meaning, importance, and functions of marketing; marketing mix (4Ps); customer services (pre and after-sales); sales promotion methods (trade fairs, exhibitions, personal selling).

topics.title: 13. Legal Aspects of Business and Consumer Protection
topics.notes: Elements of contract and agency; Sale of Goods Act and Hire Purchase Act; employer/employee obligations; business registration, patents, trademarks, copyrights; consumer protection (need, means, government legislation like Food and Drugs Act, SON, Price Control).

topics.title: 14. Government Policies and Business Management
topics.notes: Commercialization, privatization, and deregulation; business management objectives, resources (man, money, materials, goodwill), organizational structure (charts, delegation, span of control), business environment, social responsibility, and internal communication.

topics.title: 15. International Economic Groupings
topics.notes: History, membership, objectives, achievements, and challenges of ECOWAS, Niger Basin Commission, Lake Chad Basin Commission, Mano River Union, European Union, and West African Clearing House.

references: M. O. Odedokun, P. C. Udokogu & C. O. N. Oguji — Senior Secondary Commerce, Books 1, 2 & 3
E. McCarthy Jerome & Jr. William Perreault — Basic Marketing
G. B. Giles — Marketing (The M & E Handbook Series)
Prof. Achumba — Consumer Behaviour (University of Lagos)
